stories.headline: China's CXMT Q1 Profit Soars 1,688% to $3.6B as Global Memory Crunch Tightens

key_facts.fact: ChangXin Memory Technologies reported Q1 2026 revenue up roughly 719% year-on-year to about $7.5 billion, with net profit up 1,688% to $3.6 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: China's CXMT logs 1,688% profit surge amid global memory crunch

key_facts.fact: CXMT cited Omdia data placing it fourth in global DRAM with a 7.67% share, up from a low-single-digit share a year earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: Omdia ranks it No. 4 in DRAM with a 7.67% global share

key_facts.fact: The company forecast first-half 2026 revenue of 110-120 billion yuan, driven by expanded output, higher DRAM prices and an improved product mix.
key_facts.excerpt: Changxin Memory Technologies (CXMT) has forecasted its first-half revenue of between 110 and 120 billion yuan

key_facts.fact: CXMT is preparing a Shanghai STAR Market IPO targeting roughly CNY 29.5 billion (US$4.2 billion), drawing significant interest from foreign investors.
key_facts.excerpt: The company's initial public offering is attracting significant attention from foreign investors and industry observers.

sources.title: China's CXMT logs 1,688% profit surge amid global memory crunch

stories.headline: Samsung Shares Jump 6.7% as Court Curbs Union Strike and Wage Talks Resume

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics shares climbed as much as 6.7% in Seoul on May 18 after the company entered last-minute wage negotiations with its largest union, aimed at averting an 18-day strike scheduled to begin May 21.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung's shares climbed as much as 6.7% in Seoul, reversing earlier losses.

key_facts.fact: The Suwon District Court on May 18 largely granted Samsung's injunction request, ordering the union to maintain normal staffing and operations during any strike and barring it from occupying company facilities.
key_facts.excerpt: A court on Monday largely granted Samsung Electronics' request for an injunction against a general strike threatened by its unionized workers

key_facts.fact: Each of Samsung's two main unions faces a 100 million won ($66,500) per-day penalty if it violates the restrictions; the planned walkout would involve about 50,000 workers.
key_facts.excerpt: the two unions must pay 100 million won ($66,500) each per day in the event of any violation of such restrictions

key_facts.fact: Samsung produces roughly one-third of the world's DRAM and is one of only three suppliers of high-bandwidth memory used in AI accelerators, alongside SK Hynix and Micron.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung makes about a third of the world's DRAM... Samsung and SK Hynix are two of only three companies that make HBM at all; the third being American semiconductor company Micron.

key_facts.fact: Samsung began mass-producing and shipping sixth-generation HBM4 memory, with the company expecting total HBM sales to more than triple in 2026 versus 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics has begun mass-producing and shipping sixth-generation high-bandwidth memory chips, HBM4... The company expects its total HBM sales to more than triple in 2026 compared to 2025.

stories.headline: SK Hynix Sells Out 2026 HBM Capacity and Poaches 200 Samsung Engineers in Four Months

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix has sold out its entire 2026 high-bandwidth memory capacity and recruited about 200 engineers from Samsung over the past four months.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Hynix has sold out all 2026 HBM capacity for 2026, while simultaneously poaching 200 engineers from Samsung in four months.

key_facts.fact: Nomura Securities reclassified SK Hynix from a cyclical chip producer to a structural beneficiary of the AI build-out and projected 120% upside in the stock, which is up 169% year-to-date.
key_facts.excerpt: Nomura Securities predicting a 120% upside due to AI memory demand exceeding supply growth... Nomura also reclassified SK Hynix from a cyclical chip producer to a structural beneficiary of the artificial-intelligence build-out.

key_facts.fact: Samsung's HBM4 yield is reported below 60% while SK Hynix is already hitting 80% on its 1c DRAM process, with hyperscaler customers being locked into three-to-five-year supply agreements.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung's HBM4 yield sits below 60%, while SK Hynix already hits 80% on its 1c DRAM process... increasingly securing hyperscaler customers into three-to-five-year supply agreements.

key_facts.fact: Demand for specialized AI memory components is forecast to grow roughly a thousandfold over the next five years versus global supply expanding around 30% annually.
key_facts.excerpt: The demand for specialized AI memory components is forecast to increase a thousandfold over the next five years, while global supply is expanding at an estimated 30% annually.

stories.headline: GDS-Linked DayOne Plans $5B Dual IPO on Singapore and Nasdaq at ~$20B Valuation

key_facts.fact: DayOne, the international spinoff of China's largest data center operator GDS Holdings, is planning a simultaneous Singapore and US listing to raise about $5 billion, according to the Financial Times.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese data centre spin-off plans dual IPO in Singapore and US

key_facts.fact: The listing would be one of the first to use Singapore Exchange's new Global Listing Board, which lets companies with at least $2 billion market cap list on both exchanges using a single prospectus; DayOne is expected to debut at around $20 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: this listing will likely be one of the first under the so-called Global Listing Board (GLB), which lets companies with a market cap of at least $2 billion list on both exchanges using the same prospectus. Singapore-headquartered DayOne... is expected to have a market cap of US$20 billion with the IPO.

key_facts.fact: DayOne operates roughly 480MW of in-service or under-construction data center capacity plus another 590MW reserved for development across Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia and Singapore.
key_facts.excerpt: DayOne's portfolio of assets includes some 480 megawatts of data centre capacity that are in service or under construction and an additional 590 MW reserved for future development across strategic locations in Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia and Singapore

key_facts.fact: DayOne raised $2 billion in a Series C in January led by Coatue, with backers including the Indonesia Investment Authority; JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, Bank of America and Citigroup are working on the IPO.
key_facts.excerpt: DayOne, which raised more than $2 billion in its latest funding round in January, could be valued at $20 billion in the IPO... DayOne had asked JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley to lead the planned share sale and Bank of America and Citigroup to work on the deal.

stories.headline: Apple Doubles MacBook Neo Order, Books New A18 Pro Run as Binned-Chip Strategy Hits Limits

key_facts.fact: Apple is repurposing chips with partially defective cores — chips initially built for iPhones — for cheaper devices such as the $599 MacBook Neo, one of dozens of Apple products that use lower-performing processors.
key_facts.excerpt: The company's popular, $599 Neo laptop is just one of dozens of Apple devices that use lower-performing processors.

key_facts.fact: Apple has now placed new A18 Pro orders with TSMC after demand for the MacBook Neo doubled the initial production target to about 10 million units, exhausting the supply of binned chips left over from the iPhone 16 Pro.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple now plans to make about 10 million MacBook Neos in total, about twice as many as it initially ordered. This will entail its chip supplier TSMC manufacturing a new run of A18 Pro chips to power the machines

key_facts.fact: The MacBook Neo uses A18 Pro chips with five working GPU cores instead of six, salvaged from production yields that did not meet iPhone 16 Pro specifications.
key_facts.excerpt: The iPhone 16 Pro featured an A18 Pro with six GPU cores. Rather than simply discard the chips that had one defective core, Apple kept them in storage and used them inside the MacBook Neo, which is advertised as being powered by an A18 Pro chip with five GPU cores.

sources.title: Apple Is Making Hit Products and High Profits From Imperfect Chips
Report: Apple kicks off new run of A18 Pro chips as MacBook Neo demand exceeds expectations

stories.headline: Tata Electronics and ASML Sign Pact to Equip India's First $11B Commercial Chip Fab

key_facts.fact: Tata Electronics and ASML signed a strategic partnership for ASML to supply its lithography tools, training and supply-chain support to ramp Tata's first front-end semiconductor fab in Dholera, Gujarat.
key_facts.excerpt: ASML will enable the establishment and ramp-up of Tata Electronics' Dholera fab with its holistic suite of lithography tools and solutions

key_facts.fact: Tata Electronics is investing about $11 billion in the 300mm Dholera plant, which is designed to produce chips for AI, automotive and mobile applications.
key_facts.excerpt: Tata Electronics is developing the plant in Dholera, Gujarat, with ‌an investment of $11 billion, aimed at producing chips for applications ranging from automotive and mobile devices to AI

key_facts.fact: The signing was witnessed by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten as part of Modi's Netherlands visit on May 16.
key_facts.excerpt: The signing of the agreement between Tata and ASML was witnessed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Netherlands PM Rob Jetten.

key_facts.fact: India has eight semiconductor projects underway, including a separate $14 billion Tata Electronics facility in Gujarat, as the country pursues a domestic chip industry.
key_facts.excerpt: India has pledged billions of ‌dollars in subsidies to attract ​semiconductor fabrication plants ​and related manufacturing, with eight projects underway including a $14 billion Tata Electronics facility in Gujarat.
